behaviour_preservation.requirement: TEEG_10 section 3.3: the shipped default configuration must resolve to exactly the strings currently hard-coded, byte for byte. Anything else is S0.6 silently FIXING the Colab-dependence defect rather than externalising it, and TEEG_00 section 3 forbids that.
behaviour_preservation.proof_1_value_equality: For each occurrence in s06_transform_log.json, resolve(key) equals the recorded prior literal, as a string comparison on exact bytes.
behaviour_preservation.proof_2_invertibility: STRONGER, and the one that matters. The log records per occurrence the exact prior line bytes and the exact replacement line bytes, and per file the inserted import. Applying that inverse to the bytes on disk reproduces sha256_before exactly. Value equality proves the five lines are right; invertibility proves NOTHING ELSE IN THE FILE CHANGED, which value equality cannot see.
behaviour_preservation.what_is_NOT_claimed: That the two edited modules now run, or import. They do not, and S0.6 does not make them. See unimportable_by_construction below.

resolver_contract.rule: Importing towards_eeg.config performs NO filesystem access. The first read happens inside load_paths(), on the first resolve() call.
resolver_contract.rationale: TEEG_10 section 4.3 justifies laziness by the call sites -- import-time file reads would make the package unimportable when the config is absent. That reasoning does not apply to the five occurrences actually in scope, which are all at MODULE scope in files that already cannot be imported, so at those sites 'use time' and 'import time' are the same instant. The property that is real, and that is asserted here, is a property of the config module's own API: towards_eeg.config must stay importable with no configuration present, because the S0.9 import-surface assertions and any future consumer depend on it.
resolver_contract.no_search_policy: No environment-variable lookup, no search path, no user-config merging, no writing. Each would be a behaviour change relative to a hard-coded literal. The `overrides` argument exists so a later stage can inject a mapping at its own call site without this module acquiring a policy.

excluded_by_declaration.reason: Colab API call, not a configurable path. '/content/drive' is the fixed mount point the google.colab runtime provides; it is not something a deployment chooses. Externalising it would create a configuration key that must never be changed, which is worse than leaving the call visible.

unimportable_by_construction.finding: H-3, new at S0.6; no document anticipates it.
unimportable_by_construction.detail: Both files carrying the externalised literals are exported Colab notebooks with executable module scope, and neither is importable -- before S0.6 or after it. towards_eeg/connectome/connectivity_buildup.py raises ModuleNotFoundError on `from google.colab import drive`; towards_eeg/connectome/usage_example.py raises NameError on an undefined `column_input` at module scope. Both carry verdict 'keep', so both are in the installed package.
unimportable_by_construction.why_s06_does_not_fix_it: Hoisting a module-scope statement into a function is a CONTENT operation. Byte-identity rule clause (2) admits only stated mechanical transforms of an ancestor, and 'restructure the module' is not one. S0 fixes no defects (TEEG_00 section 3).
unimportable_by_construction.consequence_for_s09: Smoke assertion 3, 'importlib.import_module succeeds for every module', is currently unreachable for two keep-verdict files, and no document declares an exemption. This is recorded NOW rather than discovered at S0.9, which is the trap T-16 pattern.

unimportable_by_construction.asserted_statically_not_by_importing: H-3b, found by the S0.6 mutation harness. The first version of check_13 PROVED this declaration by importing both modules in a subprocess. That is safe on a bare machine and dangerous in Colab, which is the environment TEEG_08 mandates for running these harnesses: in Colab 'from google.colab import drive' SUCCEEDS, so the import proceeds to the next module-scope statement, drive.mount(force_remount=True), which blocks on an interactive authorisation prompt -- and if authorised, executes the rest of a 69 KB notebook body including matrix construction and file writes. An exit test that hangs, or that runs its subject's notebook as a side effect, is worse than one that is merely wrong. The dynamic probe was also environment-dependent for the second file: usage_example.py raises NameError where numpy is installed and ModuleNotFoundError where it is not, so the declared cause was a property of the machine rather than of the code. check_13 is therefore STATIC: it asserts each declared blocker is still present in the AST and that both files still carry an executable module-scope body.
unimportable_by_construction.ratification: N-23, 21 July 2026: defect class O10 -- module-scope notebook body in a keep-verdict package module -- is ratified and assigned to S1/S3. S0.9's smoke assertion 3 must therefore carry a declared exemption for the two files named here rather than being expected to pass on them.

clause_3_files_changed_at_s06.rationale: S0.6 also edits its own tooling. Those edits are byte-identity rule clause (3) -- new infrastructure on which nothing pre-existing depends -- not T11.
